ownerAssignment: Existing Trello card members preserved. New proposed owners documented in descriptions; native card assignment is not exposed by connector.

sprint.title: S2-01 | Fresh checkout → client starts and builds

checkItems.name: A clean install starts the client using documented commands and a checked-in lockfile.
A teammate can open inventory, student booking and admin preview paths without a blank page; unavailable data is explained.
Production build and lint pass; the card links the PR and setup verification.

sprint.title: S2-02 | Supabase configuration → one shared client ready

checkItems.name: Environment examples list the Supabase URL and browser-safe publishable key; missing configuration produces actionable feedback.
Feature services share one configured client and one agreed access path; no active feature depends on Firebase credentials.
Privileged server keys are absent from browser code and tracked files; a harmless connectivity check is recorded.

sprint.title: S2-03 | Empty Supabase schema → constrained tables, policies and seed

checkItems.name: Repeatable migrations define auth-user ownership, protected student/admin roles, foreign keys, unique student IDs, timestamps and request/item identifiers.
The quantity and unit contract covers whole equipment/disposables and fixed-precision chemicals; migration/adapters handle the previous quantityScale representation once, with no 100× display errors.

RLS defaults to denial; students can read active inventory and their own requests, while only verified admins can read the queue. Students cannot promote themselves or change inventory/decision fields.
A safe seed supplies equipment, chemicals, a zero-stock item and an inactive item; no real personal data or uploaded pictures are required.
The schema supports atomic request-header/lines creation and a per-user unique submission key; migration instructions and the reviewed data contract are linked.

sprint.title: S2-04 | Valid registration → student account and profile created

checkItems.name: Valid registration creates one Auth identity and one linked student profile; passwords are handled by Supabase Auth, never a profile column.
The configured email-confirmation policy is honored: show a check-email state when required and do not claim an active session prematurely; the approved confirmation callback can reach login.
A partial profile failure produces a recoverable state; retries do not create orphaned or duplicate profiles.
UI/form or callable service changes are linked with a demo of the completed registration state; no admin self-selection exists.

sprint.title: S2-05 | Invalid registration → feedback without duplicate accounts

checkItems.name: Missing/invalid email or student number, mismatched passwords and the configured password-policy failures block submission with field feedback.
Existing student IDs, provider rejections and network failures leave safe form fields available for correction without exposing internal errors or credentials.
Repeated clicks show one in-flight submission; retrying cannot create a second profile for the same identity.
Verification covers invalid input, existing identity behavior, temporary failure and successful correction.

sprint.title: S2-06 | Valid credentials → session; sign-out → signed out

checkItems.name: Correct credentials create an authenticated session; incorrect/unconfirmed credentials show safe feedback and never open a protected page.
Refreshing restores the session without briefly rendering protected content as another role.
Sign-out clears the application session and cached private state; expired sessions return to the signed-out state.
A short verification covers successful login, rejection, refresh and sign-out; passwords/tokens are absent from logs.

sprint.title: S2-07 | Resolved account role → correct student or admin route

checkItems.name: Students reach inventory/booking; verified admins reach the admin queue; signed-out users reach login.
Direct admin URLs are denied to a student, including after refresh or Back navigation; a loading state waits for trusted role resolution.
Missing profiles or unsupported roles show a recoverable access state and grant no privileged default.
Only a trusted provisioning path creates the test admin; changing browser state or user-editable metadata cannot grant access.

sprint.title: S2-08 | Unauthorized data request → denied by Supabase policies

checkItems.name: A signed-out client cannot read protected profiles/requests or write inventory.
Student A cannot read/write Student B's request or profile by guessing IDs; a student cannot update their role, stock or decision status.
The test admin can read Pending request headers and lines, while students can read only their own.
Policy tests use actual non-privileged sessions against the development database; denial evidence and any policy migration are linked.

sprint.title: S2-09 | Inventory loading → active items with correct available units

checkItems.name: An authenticated student sees active seeded items with name/code, category/type, available stock, unit and availability status; inactive rows are hidden.
Equipment/disposable counts and chemical amounts follow S2-03's contract with no duplicate scaling; zero-stock items remain visible and clearly unavailable.
Loading, empty inventory and read failure are distinguishable; a failed live read never silently falls back to sample data.
A seeded database change appears after reload; read access succeeds without an admin/service key.

sprint.title: S2-10 | Search/filter change → matching inventory or no results

checkItems.name: Typing a name or code updates matching rows without needing a separate submit.
Category and In stock/Out of stock filters combine with the search; counts match the displayed results.
Clear/reset restores the active inventory; zero matches show a useful no-results state rather than a loading/error state.
Checks cover uppercase input, blank search, combined filters, zero-stock matches and reset.

sprint.title: S2-11 | Item selection changes → editable booking draft

checkItems.name: A student can select an available active item once; duplicate selection is prevented and zero-stock items cannot be added.
Changing quantities or removing an item updates the draft while preserving borrower/course/purpose/date entries.
The borrower identity comes from the session/profile; fixed units are not editable by the borrower.
Whole equipment/disposable and allowed fixed-precision chemical quantities follow the data contract; no request is saved while editing.

sprint.title: S2-12 | Invalid booking draft → errors with entered data preserved

checkItems.name: Empty selection, missing course/purpose/dates, invalid dates, zero/negative/non-finite quantities and excess precision show specific feedback.
Equipment/disposables reject fractional counts and every item respects the displayed stock limit; server recheck remains authoritative.
Validation failure creates no request and retains the draft; correcting one field clears its error appropriately.
Keyboard focus reaches the feedback and the student can correct and resubmit.

sprint.title: S2-13 | Valid booking → one saved Pending request and reference

checkItems.name: The saved header belongs to the authenticated user, starts as Pending and links every requested item/quantity/unit; the client cannot supply another owner or privileged status.
Authoritative validation rechecks active items, current stock, quantities and dates; invalid input fails without a partial header or orphaned lines.
Header and lines commit atomically with a per-user unique submission key; the confirmation appears only after success and shows a stable reference.
Reloading/querying the development database finds the saved request; no live-mode fallback claims a sample submission was saved.

sprint.title: S2-14 | Failed/repeated booking submission → safe retry

checkItems.name: An in-flight submission locks only the necessary actions; duplicate clicks send at most one active attempt.
Failure keeps the draft and offers correction/login/retry as appropriate; changed-stock feedback identifies what needs rechecking.
Retrying the same submission key after a lost response resolves to the original saved request and cannot insert duplicates.
Verification covers network failure, expired session, changed stock and committed-but-response-lost retry.

sprint.title: S2-15 | Admin queue opens → saved Pending request details

checkItems.name: A request saved by S2-13 appears for a provisioned admin after reload with requester identity, reference, dates, purpose and item quantities/units.
The queue distinguishes loading, no Pending requests and read failure; selecting an item displays its matching details.
A student cannot access the queue data even through a direct data request.
Existing mock approval buttons cannot display success in live mode; the demo proves actual database read-through, not copied fixtures.

sprint.title: S2-16 | Student-to-admin flow → reviewed Sprint 2 increment

checkItems.name: A clean checkout can register a student, honor confirmation settings, log in, browse/filter real seeded inventory, save a Pending request and find it as the test admin.
Another student and a signed-out session cannot read that request; no Firebase-only or separate fixture path is presented as the completed live flow.
Build/lint and relevant auth, RLS and request-persistence checks pass; record results, limitations and the integration commit/PR.
Complete sprint review with a demo and retrospective with one concrete improvement; unfinished scope returns to Product Backlog instead of being marked Done.
